initialContact.message: All my friends are going shopping this weekend and getting new clothes for spring. They keep showing me stuff on Instagram and TikTok. I have 160€ budgeted for spending this month but I already used 80€. If I spend another 80€ on clothes, I won't have money for anything else this month. But I don't want to be the only one not shopping. What should I tell them?

problemContext.currentSituation: Teen facing peer pressure to overspend budget on shopping trip
problemContext.emotionalState: FOMO, peer pressure, wanting to fit in, knows overspending is wrong

idealAdvice: This is tough - peer pressure about money is real, especially at 17!
Let's think through your options:
Option 1: Go shopping, spend 80€, have 0€ rest of month
- Consequence: No money for anything unexpected, no going out later this month
- Risk: What if friends want to do something else later and you're broke?
Option 2: Skip shopping, save 80€, feel left out
- Consequence: FOMO, might feel excluded
- Benefit: Still have money for activities later in month
Option 3 (Best): Go shopping with LIMITED budget
- Bring ONLY 30-40€ in cash (leave card at home)
- Go for the hangout, not the haul
- Find 1-2 pieces you love within budget
- Remaining 40-50€ available for rest of month
The social media trap:
Instagram/TikTok showing you expensive hauls creates fake 'normal'
Reality: Most people can't afford huge shopping sprees every month
Your friends posting hauls: Might be maxing out parents' cards, getting into debt, or just showing off
What to tell friends:
DON'T say: 'I can't afford it' (creates shame)
DO say: 'I'm saving for Spain trip but I'll come hang and get one thing!'
Real friends: Will respect your goals
Friends who pressure you to overspend: Not looking out for you
Perspective:
You're 17 with 850€ saved and clear goals - you're ahead of most adults!
Shopping spree now: Temporarily fun, doesn't move you toward Spain
Staying on budget: Gets you closer to life-changing experience
Future you in Spain at 19: Won't remember this shopping trip in April 2025
Future you if broke and can't afford Spain: Will regret every impulse shopping trip
The skill you're learning:
Saying 'no' to peer pressure about money at 17: Will save you thousands of euros over lifetime
This isn't about one shopping trip - it's about who you want to be with money
Quick test: Would you rather have new shirt now OR be in Spain in 18 months?
That answer tells you what to do
commonMistakes: Telling her to just not go (misses social importance)
Not offering compromise option (limited budget shopping)
Dismissing peer pressure as unimportant (it's real for teens)
Not addressing social media influence explicitly
Missing opportunity to reinforce her good savings habit
Not giving specific phrases to use with friends
